sections.content:
Now I get it! When I clicked the empty square (1,3), the two dots at (1,1) and (1,2) got merged into a single dot at (1,3)! Let me verify:
- Before the click: the dots were at (1,1), (1,2), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5), and the ring was on (1,1).
- After the click: the dots are at (1,3), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5). The ring disappeared. The dot at (1,1) disappeared (N→w at 18-20,17-20), the dot at (1,2) also disappeared (N→w at 18-20,23-26), and a new dot appeared at (1,3) (N at 18-20, 29-32).
So the mechanic is: click a dot to select it, then click another cell (or dot?) to move it. But here, two dots moved to the target? Actually, it looks like the selected dot (1,1) and the dot at (1,2) both got merged into (1,3)? Or: the selected dot moved to (1,3), and the dot at (1,2) also moved to (1,3) and they merged (2 dots in 1 cell = 1 dot?).
Hmm. Or maybe the mechanic is: click a dot to select it; click a destination; the selected dot moves there; if there's a dot at the destination... but the destination (1,3) was empty. So why did (1,2) disappear?
Wait, maybe I misread. Let me carefully re-verify the diff:
- (18,18),(18,19) N→w; (19,17..20) N→w; (20,17..20) N→w: the dot at (1,1) disappeared.
- (18,24),(18,25) N→w; (19,23..26) N→w; (20,23..26) N→w: the dot at (1,2) disappeared.
- (18,30),(18,31) g→N; (19,29..32) w/g→N; (20,29..) ...: a new dot appeared at (1,3).
- The ring G→W: the ring disappeared.
- (18,20) G→w: hmm, part of the ring overlapped.
So both dots at (1,1) and (1,2) got removed, and a single dot appeared at (1,3). This is a merge: two adjacent dots got merged into one at the clicked cell? Interesting — like a 2048-style merge: the selected dot (1,1) and its neighbor (1,2) got merged into (1,3)?
Or, the mechanic might be "click to select a dot; click a destination; all dots in the line between the source and destination get merged"? Hmm.
Another interpretation: this is a "dot merge" puzzle: click a dot, then click an adjacent/other cell, and the selected dot slides in that direction, merging with dots along the way? The selected dot (1,1) slides right: passes through (1,2) where there's a dot → merge, continues to (1,3)? But then it should stop at the merge point...
Actually, wait. Maybe the mechanic is: click a dot to select it. Click a destination cell. The selected dot moves to the destination, and any dots in the path get absorbed/merged (like a vacuum). The result is a single dot at the destination.
Or, this game might be about reducing the number of dots: the goal is to merge all 5 dots into 1? Or to place dots in specific positions?
Let me think about what the goal could be. Initial dots: (1,1), (1,2), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5). Now: (1,3), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5) — 4 dots.
Hmm, maybe the goal is to merge all dots into one? Or to place them in a specific pattern?
Let me experiment more. Current dots: (1,3), (1,4), (2,5), (4,5).
Test: click the dot at (1,3), then click (1,4) (which has a dot). If they merge into (1,4), then the mechanic is "move the selected dot to the destination, merging with the dot there."
Actually, from the previous move: the selected dot (1,1) moved to (1,3), and the dot at (1,2) in the path got absorbed. So the selected dot slides right from (1,1): absorbs the dot at (1,2), and stops at (1,3)?? Why stop at (1,3) and not continue to (1,4) where there's another dot? Because I clicked (1,3) as the destination. So: the selected dot moves to the clicked cell, absorbing any dots along the straight-line path.
So the mechanic: click a dot → select (ring). Click a cell (probably in the same row/column) → the dot moves there, absorbing any dots in between.
Goal: probably to merge all dots into one? Or to reach a specific configuration?
Hmm, wait, but actually the absorption might be a merge: two dots become one. So the count decreases. 5 dots → 4 dots.
Maybe the goal is: reduce to 1 dot? Or the goal is to place dots in specific "target" cells (the darkened g squares?). The darkening of (1,3) before the click was... wait, (1,3) was already darkened (g) before I clicked. Interesting! So (1,3) was a target cell, and clicking it placed/merged the dot there.
Hmm, but why did (1,3) get darkened when I clicked the dot at (1,1)? Maybe clicking a dot highlights its "target" cell? That is, each dot has a target, and clicking a dot shows where it should go? And clicking that target moves the dot there (absorbing dots in the path)?
Let me test: click the dot at (1,3) and see if a target appears (some cell gets darkened). Then click that target.
Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the darkening of (1,3) was a preview of "if you click here, the dot will move here." That is, clicking a dot highlights the allowed destination cells? But only one cell got darkened: (1,3). If it were showing all allowed destinations, more cells should have darkened.
Let me probe: click the dot at (1,3) (center (19,30)).
